disease_label_per_paper: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma diagnosed antemortem by transbronchial lung biopsy and multiple random skin biopsies
presentation_summary: Previously healthy man with 3 months of high fever, nocturnal sweating, exertional dyspnea, dry cough/hypoxemia, and radiologic lung abnormalities refractory to antibiotics and pulse methylprednisolone followed by prednisolone
Laboratory testing showed WBC 11000/uL, ALT 83 U/L, surfactant protein D 132 ng/mL, LDH 605 U/L, CRP 19.5 mg/dL, procalcitonin 9.6 ng/mL, and soluble IL-2 receptor 2320 U/mL
Aggressive multiple random skin biopsies and transbronchial lung biopsy made antemortem IVLBCL diagnosis

observations.source_text_value: dry cough described among respiratory symptoms in reviewed TBLB-diagnosed IVLBCL cases
respiratory symptoms and persistent fever were refractory to antibiotics
radiological patterns included ground glass opacities, centrilobular nodules, interlobular septal thickening, interstitial shadows, and bronchovascular bundle thickening

confirmatory_findings.finding: abundant CD20 atypical lymphocytes aggregated in lumina of small vessels

exclusion_notes: Biopsy positivity is confirmatory and should not be used as ordinary presentation-time evidence in diagnostic ranking.
